This chunk is about:
- People: Warren G. Harding, Nan Britton, Elizabeth
- Roles: President of the United States, United States Senator, secretary, mistress
- Events: Harding presidency, Harding's death, Teapot Dome scandal, 1927 paternity revelation

Facts:
- Warren G. Harding was born on November 2, 1865, and he later became the 29th President of the United States.
- Nan Britton, born Nanna Popham Britton on November 9, 1896, was an American secretary and the mistress of Warren G. Harding.
- Warren G. Harding served as the 29th President of the United States from March 4, 1921, until his death on August 2, 1923.
- At the time of his death in 1923, Warren G. Harding was one of the most popular presidents.
- After Warren G. Harding's death, public regard for him declined because scandals from his administration, including Teapot Dome, became known.
- After Warren G. Harding's death, revelations about his affair with Nan Britton also damaged his reputation.
- In 1927, Nan Britton revealed that her daughter Elizabeth had been fathered by Warren G. Harding while he was serving in the United States Senate, one year before he was elected president.
